- Coste: gasto por intereses 350 (2024: 340); intereses sobre pasivos por arrendamiento (465) (2024: (422)); ingreso por intereses 159 (2024: 221); gasto financiero neto 647 (2024: 562). [AD_annual-report-2025.txt, PDF p. 227]
- Intereses pagados 261; intereses cobrados 130; amortización de pasivos por arrendamiento 1.944 (2024: 1.743). [AD_annual-report-2025.txt, PDF p. 56]
- Coste medio ponderado de la deuda como cifra publicada: No encontrado en los documentos.
- Pasivos por arrendamiento: 11.974 millones (corriente 1.448; no corriente 10.526); 2024: 12.253. Pagos no descontados 14.721 (2024: 15.080): dentro de un año 1.879; de uno a cinco años 6.514; de cinco a diez 4.061; de diez a quince 1.571; más de quince 695. [AD_annual-report-2025.txt, PDF p. 271]
- Salidas potenciales no incluidas en el pasivo por prórrogas no consideradas razonablemente ciertas: unos 35.000 millones sin descontar (2024: 40.000 millones). [AD_annual-report-2025.txt, PDF p. 272]
- Cuotas variables de arrendamiento: normalmente entre 1 % y 6 % de las ventas netas de la tienda. [AD_annual-report-2025.txt, PDF p. 272]
- Gasto por depreciación de derechos de uso 1.400 (2024: 1.333); salida total de caja por arrendamientos 2.001 (2024: 1.808). [AD_annual-report-2025.txt, PDF p. 272, 273]
- La empresa dice que ningún arrendamiento impone restricciones al pago de dividendos, a nueva deuda ni a nuevos arrendamientos. [AD_annual-report-2025.txt, PDF p. 272]
- Proporción de ubicaciones: 8.152 locales minoristas propios o arrendados, 15 % en propiedad y 85 % arrendados; 942 subarrendados a franquiciados. [AD_annual-report-2025.txt, PDF p. 58]
- Pensiones y otros beneficios posteriores al empleo: 504 millones (2024: 553), con obligaciones de beneficio definido 183 y otras obligaciones a largo plazo 321; más 50 en no corriente y 50 en corriente por la liquidación del plan neerlandés. Activos por pensiones 70. [AD_annual-report-2025.txt, PDF p. 53, 248]
- Gasto total de pensiones 2025: 805 (2024: 1.018), con planes de aportación definida 378 y planes multiempleador de beneficio definido 66 y de aportación definida 292. [AD_annual-report-2025.txt, PDF p. 248]
- Planes multiempleador: siete de beneficio definido y 37 de aportación definida. [AD_annual-report-2025.txt, PDF p. 253, 255]
- Intereses minoritarios: cero en resultado y en resultado global. [AD_annual-report-2025.txt, PDF p. 212, 213]
- Financiación de proveedores: cuentas a pagar bajo acuerdos de financiación de la cadena de suministro 1.396 (2024: 1.286); cuentas a pagar totales 9.009. [AD_annual-report-2025.txt, PDF p. 263]
- Pérdidas fiscales acumuladas: 1.067 millones nominales (2024: 1.439). [AD_annual-report-2025.txt, PDF p. 230]
- Reparto de caja 2025: dividendos 1.070 (2024: 1.037); recompra 1.008 (2024: 1.000). Acciones en circulación 887 millones (2024: 914); acciones propias 4.311 miles. [AD_annual-report-2025.txt, PDF p. 56, 62, 65]
- Efectivo de operaciones continuadas 6.989 (2024: 6.224); flujo de caja libre 2.600 (2024: 2.545). [AD_annual-report-2025.txt, PDF p. 56]


### (2026) Posterior al cierre de 2025
- (2026) Deuda neta: 15.467 (29 de marzo de 2026); 15.961 (28 de junio de 2026); 16.087 (27 de septiembre de 2026) frente a 14.699 al cierre de 2025. Deuda bruta 19.747 (27 de septiembre) frente a 18.404: préstamos 4.854 (4.577), arrendamientos 10.572 (10.526), corto plazo y parte corriente 4.321 (3.301). Efectivo y similares 3.660 (3.705). [AD_q2-2026-interim-report.txt, PDF p. 23] [AD_q3-2026-interim-report.txt, PDF p. 24]
- (2026) Variación de deuda neta en el 3T: +126 millones, por dividendos de 445 y recompra de 285, compensados por flujo de caja libre de 445 y una baja de pasivos por arrendamiento y otros efectos de 159. En el 2T: +494 millones. [AD_q3-2026-interim-report.txt, PDF p. 10] [AD_q2-2026-interim-report.txt, PDF p. 9]
- (2026) Cash pooling nocional: 1.176 millones (28 de junio: 600; 28 de diciembre de 2025: 590), compensado en deuda a corto. [AD_q3-2026-interim-report.txt, PDF p. 24]
- (2026) Emisión del 5 de marzo de 2026 (liquidada el 12 de marzo): 800 millones en dos tramos: 300 millones a dos años a tipo variable (Euribor 3M + 35 pb) y 500 millones verdes a ocho años, precio 99,884 %, cupón 3,625 %. Flujo de efectivo: ingresos por deuda a largo 816 y amortización de préstamos (914) en 39 semanas. [AD_q3-2026-interim-report.txt, PDF p. 16, 21]
- (2026) Flujo de caja libre: 2T 632 (517); 1S 302 (715); 3T 445 (389); 39 semanas 747 (1.104). La empresa atribuye la caída del acumulado al capital circulante por el calendario y la estacionalidad, y la guía del año a ~2.100 millones al incidente de ciberseguridad y a nuevas normas de pago a proveedores en Serbia. [AD_q2-2026-interim-report.txt, PDF p. 9] [AD_q3-2026-interim-report.txt, PDF p. 2, 10, 24]
- (2026) Gasto financiero neto: 3T (183) (155); 39 semanas (545) (481); intereses sobre arrendamientos 3T (116) y acumulado (350) (349); gasto de intereses acumulado (259) (266). [AD_q3-2026-interim-report.txt, PDF p. 12]
- (2026) Dividendos: final de 2025 de 0,73 € pagado el 23 de abril de 2026 (la Junta aprobó el dividendo de 1,24 € el 8 de abril de 2026); dividendo intermedio de 2026 de 0,51 € (igual que 2025) anunciado el 5 de agosto y pagado el 27 de agosto de 2026. Dividendos pagados en 39 semanas: 1.088. [AD_q2-2026-interim-report.txt, PDF p. 2, 20] [AD_q3-2026-interim-report.txt, PDF p. 16, 21]
- (2026) Recompra del programa de 1.000 millones (iniciado el 29 de diciembre de 2025, a completar antes de fin de 2026): 23.847.837 acciones a un precio medio de 35,41 € en los tres primeros trimestres (1S: 15.257.549 acciones a 36,97 €); 844 millones en tres trimestres (3T: 8,6 millones de acciones por 280 millones; 2T: 9,0 millones por 340 millones); efectivo de recompra en 39 semanas 864. Acciones en circulación: 865.173.863 (27 de septiembre de 2026), frente a 886.877.259 al cierre de 2025. [AD_q2-2026-interim-report.txt, PDF p. 6, 20] [AD_q3-2026-interim-report.txt, PDF p. 6, 16, 21]
- (2026) Nota de la empresa en la tabla de guía: los programas de recompra y dividendo pueden ajustarse ante operaciones corporativas, incluidas fusiones y adquisiciones significativas. [AD_q3-2026-interim-report.txt, PDF p. 9, 30]
- (2026) Patrimonio atribuido a accionistas: 14.375 (27 de septiembre de 2026) frente a 14.195. Pensiones y otros beneficios posteriores al empleo: 471 (504). Provisiones no corrientes 886. Pasivo por impuestos diferidos 1.245. Intereses minoritarios: cero. [AD_q3-2026-interim-report.txt, PDF p. 14, 12]
- (2026) Liquidación de pensiones en EE. UU.: la partida de reestructuración y otros fue de (21) millones en el 3T (ganancia), principalmente por esa liquidación; el resultado IFRS del 3T fue 30 millones mayor que el subyacente. [AD_q3-2026-interim-report.txt, PDF p. 10]
- (2026) Litigio por opioides (MDL n.º 2804): la empresa sigue en mediación con los demandantes y fiscales generales estatales, cree tener defensas sólidas y no puede predecir el resultado. [AD_q2-2026-interim-report.txt, PDF p. 22] [AD_q3-2026-interim-report.txt, PDF p. 23]
- (2026) Calificaciones crediticias en 2026: No encontrado en los documentos (los informes intermedios no las mencionan).

## 7. Regulación y capital
No aplica: no es una entidad financiera ni regulada en capital.

## 8. Hechos medibles para predicciones
Último valor publicado, cierre de 2025 salvo indicación:
- Tiendas 9.551 (EE. UU. 2.017; Europa 7.534); operadas por la empresa 7.199; por franquiciados 2.352. Puntos de recogida 1.931 (EE. UU. 1.670; Europa 261). Locales minoristas propios o arrendados 8.152. [AD_annual-report-2025.txt, PDF p. 58]
- Serie de número de tiendas: 6.556 (1 de enero de 2017), 6.637, 6.769, 6.967, 7.137, 7.452, 7.659, 7.716, 7.765, 9.551 (2025). [AD_annual-report-2025.txt, PDF p. 65]
- Clientes semanales 77 millones; marcas 17; asociados 384.000 (cabezas) y 222.000 (FTE); empleados en 2024: 388.000. [AD_annual-report-2025.txt, PDF p. 12, 65]
- Ventas netas 92.352; resultado operativo subyacente 3.734; margen subyacente 4,0 %; EBITDA subyacente 7.319. [AD_annual-report-2025.txt, PDF p. 42]
- Ventas comparables sin gasolina, Grupo: 3,2 % (2025; 86.680 frente a 84.004 millones); EE. UU. 3,0 %; Europa 3,4 %. [AD_annual-report-2025.txt, PDF p. 344, 49]
- Ventas online 10.274; EE. UU. 4.637; Europa 5.637. [AD_annual-report-2025.txt, PDF p. 343]
- Racha de ventas comparables positivas: Food Lion 53 trimestres; Hannaford 18 trimestres. [AD_annual-report-2025.txt, PDF p. 43, 50]
- Albert Heijn: 38,2 % de cuota; séptimo año consecutivo ganando cuota. [AD_annual-report-2025.txt, PDF p. 50]
- Save for Our Customers 1.294 millones. [AD_annual-report-2025.txt, PDF p. 45]
- Ofertas personalizadas en EE. UU.: más de 14.200 millones, +18 % interanual; suscriptores de Albert Heijn Premium: más de un millón. [AD_annual-report-2025.txt, PDF p. 28]
- Alimentos de marca propia saludables: 52,1 % de las ventas de alimentos de marca propia a tipo constante (2024: 52,4 %). [AD_annual-report-2025.txt, PDF p. 7, 130]
- BPA subyacente diluido 2,67 € (2024: 2,54); BPA diluido de operaciones continuadas 2,50 € (2024: 1,89). Acciones diluidas medias para el BPA subyacente: 905 millones (2024: 933). [AD_annual-report-2025.txt, PDF p. 48, 343]
- Dividendo por acción: 0,76 (2019), 0,90 (2020), 0,95 (2021), 1,05 (2022), 1,10 (2023), 1,17 (2024), 1,24 (2025). Payout 47 % (2025), 46 %, 43 %, 40 %, 42 %. [AD_annual-report-2025.txt, PDF p. 63, 64]
- Flujo de caja libre (millones): 1.441 (2016), 1.926, 2.165, 1.843, 2.199, 1.618, 2.188, 2.425, 2.545, 2.600 (2025). [AD_annual-report-2025.txt, PDF p. 64]
- Crecimiento de ventas a tipo constante 2016 a 2025: 32,3 %, 28,9 %, 2,5 %, 2,3 %, 12,3 %, 5,0 %, 6,9 %, 3,9 %, 0,9 %, 5,9 %. [AD_annual-report-2025.txt, PDF p. 64]
- Ventas netas (millones): 49.695 (2016), 62.890, 62.791, 66.260, 74.736, 75.601, 86.984, 88.734, 89.356, 92.352. [AD_annual-report-2025.txt, PDF p. 64]
- Deuda neta 14.699; capitalización bursátil a cierre 30.659 millones; precio de cierre 34,57 €; máximo 38,01 € (22 de mayo de 2025); mínimo 31,29 € (30 de diciembre de 2025). [AD_annual-report-2025.txt, PDF p. 61, 65]
- Rentabilidad por dividendo 3,6 % (2025). [AD_annual-report-2025.txt, PDF p. 63]
- Tasa efectiva de impuestos 22,4 % (2024: 21,7 %). [AD_annual-report-2025.txt, PDF p. 46]
- Resultado de empresas conjuntas y asociadas 18 (2024: 23); participación en JMR 49 % y Super Indo 51 %, sin consolidar. [AD_annual-report-2025.txt, PDF p. 46, 279]
- Gasto de compensación en acciones: 70 (2024: 42); EE. UU. 37, Europa 18, Group 14. [AD_annual-report-2025.txt, PDF p. 224]


### (2026) Posterior al cierre de 2025
- (2026) Tiendas: 9.832 (27 de septiembre de 2026; EE. UU. 2.021; Europa 7.811); especializadas (Etos y Gall & Gall) 1.129. [AD_q3-2026-interim-report.txt, PDF p. 11]
- (2026) Ventas comparables sin gasolina, 3T: Grupo 1,2 %; EE. UU. 0,5 %; Europa 2,1 %. Ventas netas 3T 23.089. [AD_q3-2026-interim-report.txt, PDF p. 3]
- (2026) Online 3T: ventas 2.628; EE. UU. +14,2 % a tipo constante (décimo trimestre consecutivo de dos dígitos); retención online EE. UU. superior al 75 % trimestre a trimestre; Food Lion crece más de 20 % online. [AD_q3-2026-interim-report.txt, PDF p. 3, 4, 7]
- (2026) Margen subyacente 3T: Grupo 4,1 %; EE. UU. 4,3 %; Europa 4,0 %. [AD_q3-2026-interim-report.txt, PDF p. 3]
- (2026) BPA subyacente diluido 3T 0,69 € (+1,4 % a tipo constante); BPA diluido de operaciones continuadas 0,72 €; 39 semanas: 1,95 € y 1,93 €. [AD_q3-2026-interim-report.txt, PDF p. 3, 6]
- (2026) Flujo de caja libre 3T 445; 39 semanas 747. Deuda neta 16.087. [AD_q3-2026-interim-report.txt, PDF p. 3, 24]
- (2026) Acciones medias ponderadas diluidas 3T: 872 millones (902 en 3T 2025). [AD_q3-2026-interim-report.txt, PDF p. 12]
- (2026) Albert (Chequia): 38 trimestres consecutivos de ventas comparables positivas (2T de 2026). [AD_q2-2026-interim-report.txt, PDF p. 4]
- (2026) Penetración de marca propia de alimentos del Grupo: más de 40 % (2T de 2026). [AD_q2-2026-interim-report.txt, PDF p. 4]
- (2026) Comparable sales de 3T 2025 como base de comparación: EE. UU. 2,9 %; Europa 2,8 %. [AD_q3-2026-interim-report.txt, PDF p. 7, 8]
- (2026) Equipo directivo que firma los informes intermedios: 2T (4 de agosto de 2026) Muller, Poots-Bijl y Sarrailh (CEO Europa e Indonesia); 3T (3 de noviembre de 2026) Muller, Poots-Bijl, Claire Peters (CEO Ahold Delhaize USA) y Margaret Versteden-van Duijn (CEO Europa e Indonesia). Los informes mencionan «medidas para respaldar transiciones efectivas en funciones clave de liderazgo». Se consigna como hecho, sin interpretación. [AD_q2-2026-interim-report.txt, PDF p. 10, 29] [AD_q3-2026-interim-report.txt, PDF p. 11, 30]

## 9. Lo que no encontré
- Entrada de la etapa 1: el archivo etapa1/extracto.md no existe en la carpeta; el texto de etapa 1 disponible es etapa1/Ahold_respuesta.md y se usó solo para no repetir. La carpeta texto/ contiene los informes anuales 2016 a 2025 y, desde esta actualización, los informes intermedios del 2T de 2026 (5 de agosto de 2026) y del 3T de 2026 (4 de noviembre de 2026). Los datos de 2026 están marcados «(2026)»; son posteriores al cierre de 2025 y no están auditados.
- Convención de páginas: todas las citas usan la marca [PDF PAGE n] del texto; la página impresa del informe es una menos que la marca.
- Tamaño de mercado (valor) y crecimiento del mercado como cifra de la empresa, por país o región.
- Definición y mercado de referencia de la cuota de Albert Heijn (38,2 %); cuota de mercado de cualquier otra marca, incluidas las de EE. UU.
- Cifra de cuota de Delhaize (solo «récord»).
- Competidores nombrados como tales: no aparecen; los nombres en los documentos son grupos de comparación de retribución y de rentabilidad para el accionista.
- Importe y porcentaje de ventas de I+D.
- Capex por destino con importe (reformas, centros de distribución, tecnología); solo hay capex por región.
- Múltiplo pagado por Profi y precio de Delfood.
- Retorno esperado del centro de distribución de Carolina del Norte, de las reformas y del arrendamiento de Blackstone.
- Desglose del efecto de precio, volumen y mezcla en las ventas comparables; cifra de volumen de 2025.
- Valores de penetración de compra online de alimentación de 2025 en EE. UU. y Europa: el gráfico existe pero las cifras no se pueden asignar con fiabilidad en el texto convertido. [AD_annual-report-2025.txt, PDF p. 44]
- Margen por marca (Stop & Shop, Food Lion, Albert Heijn, etc.) y ventas por marca; solo hay segmentos EE. UU. y Europa.
- Reparto de ventas por país salvo Países Bajos y EE. UU.; el resto agrupado como «resto del mundo».
- Coste medio ponderado de la deuda y tipo medio ponderado de descuento de los arrendamientos como cifra publicada.
- Ratio de apalancamiento real frente al covenant de 5,5:1 (no se calcula porque no se comprueba).
- Serie publicada de ROIC o ROCE para la empresa.
- Valor de la partida de Palancas!C24 (tamaño del mercado año 10): no hay cifra de fuente primaria en los textos.
- Operaciones de directivos y consejeros como serie: No encontrado en los textos de los informes anuales revisados.
- Regulación y capital (sección 7): no aplica.
- (2026) Precio de Delfood; múltiplo de Tesco Chequia y Eslovaquia sobre ventas o resultado, y las ventas y el resultado de esa empresa: No encontrado en los documentos.
- (2026) Calificaciones crediticias vigentes en 2026 y covenants probados en 2026: No encontrado en los documentos.
- (2026) Ventas y resultados del 4T de 2026 y efecto real del incidente de ciberseguridad (solo estimaciones del 3T): No encontrado en los documentos.
- (2026) Cifras de cuota de mercado de 2026 (solo declaraciones de ganancia de cuota, y Nielsen del 1T de 2026 sin cifra).
- (2026) Desglose de precio, volumen y mezcla en 2026: solo impactos en puntos porcentuales por factores (SNAP, huevos, farmacia, clima); sin cifra de volumen.
- (2026) Motivo de los cambios de firmantes de la declaración de la dirección: No encontrado en los documentos.

Legal proceedings
Ahold Delhaize and certain of its former or current subsidiaries are involved in a number of
legal proceedings, which include litigation as a result of divestments, tax and employment, as
well as other litigation and inquiries. The legal proceedings discussed below, whether pending,
threatened or unasserted, if decided adversely or settled, may result in liability material to
Ahold Delhaize’s financial condition, results of operations or cash flows. Ahold Delhaize may
enter into discussions regarding the settlement of these and other proceedings, and may enter
into settlement agreements, if it believes settlement is in the best interest of Ahold Delhaize’s
shareholders. In accordance with IAS 37 “Provisions, Contingent Liabilities, and Contingent
Assets,” Ahold Delhaize has recognized provisions with respect to these proceedings,
where appropriate, which are reflected on its balance sheet.
National prescription opiate litigation
Several U.S. brands and subsidiaries of Ahold Delhaize have been sued in a number of lawsuits
included in In re: National Prescription Opiate Litigation (MDL No. 2804), a multi-district litigation
(MDL) matter pending in the United States District Court in the Northern District of Ohio. The MDL
contains thousands of cases filed against hundreds of defendants by counties, cities, hospitals
and others concerning the impact of opioid abuse. Several U.S. brands and subsidiaries of Ahold
Delhaize also have been sued in a number of lawsuits pending in courts in New York, which
are not part of the MDL. The MDL and New York suits name Ahold Delhaize as a defendant, as
well as various subsidiaries, including American Sales Company LLC, which ceased operations
prior to being named as a defendant in any MDL-related case. Although the MDL matters in
which Ahold Delhaize or its subsidiaries have been named have been stayed by the court and,
therefore, are not being actively litigated at this time, the court has requested status reports
in many stayed cases (including those in which Ahold Delhaize and its subsidiaries have been
named). The New York matters in which Ahold Delhaize or its subsidiaries have been named
are also currently stayed. Ahold Delhaize and its subsidiaries are exchanging dispensing
information and potential frameworks for resolution with Plaintiffs' counsel and the Attorneys
General of various states in which they operate. The Company continues to believe there are
strong factual and legal defenses to the plaintiffs’ claims. Ahold Delhaize is not currently able
to predict the outcome of these claims.
Other legal proceedings
In addition to the legal proceedings described previously in this Note, Ahold Delhaize and
its former or current subsidiaries are parties to a number of other legal proceedings arising
out of their business operations. Ahold Delhaize believes that the ultimate resolution of these
other proceedings will not, in the aggregate, have a material adverse effect on Ahold Delhaize’s
financial position, results of operations or cash flows. Such other legal proceedings, however,
are subject to inherent uncertainties, and the outcome of individual matters is unpredictable.
It is possible that Ahold Delhaize could be required to make expenditures, in excess
of established provisions, in amounts that cannot reasonably be estimated.

 Ahold Delhaize reports resilient Q2 2026 results and reiterates guidance for the year

* Anchored by the strong execution of our Growing Together strategy, we delivered a resilient performance
 in the second quarter. Through disciplined investments in our customer value propositions, innovation
 and growth, combined with strong cost management, we strengthened our market positions and gained
 share across our major markets and brands in an uncertain macroeconomic environment.
* Q2 net sales were €23.2 billion, up 1.9% at constant exchange rates and up 0.3% at actual exchange
 rates.
* Q2 comparable sales excluding gasoline increased 0.8% in the U.S. They were negatively impacted by
 0.1 percentage points due to calendar shifts and 0.7 percentage points due to pharmacy pricing related to
 the Inflation Reduction Act. Deflation in egg prices and lower Supplementary Nutrition Assistance
 Program (SNAP) benefits from program changes had a negative impact of 0.9 percentage points.
* Q2 comparable sales excluding gasoline increased 1.7% in Europe. Calendar shifts had a negative
 impact of 0.1 percentage points.
* Ahold Delhaize's online sales increased 8.6% in Q2 at constant exchange rates and 7.3% at actual
 exchange rates. This was driven by strong growth of 14.5% at constant exchange rates in the U.S.,
 where customers continue to appreciate the convenience, assortments and personalization offered by our
 online shopping experiences, supported by our strong omnichannel model.
* Q2 underlying operating margin was 3.9%, a decrease of 0.1 percentage points at constant exchange
 rates. Improvements in Europe were more than offset by a modest decline in the U.S.
* Q2 diluted underlying earnings per share (EPS) was €0.63, a decrease of 1.4% compared to the prior
 year at constant exchange rates.
* Q2 IFRS operating income was €866 million and IFRS-diluted EPS from continuing operations was
 €0.60.
* The 2026 interim dividend is €0.51 (2025: €0.51), based on the Group's dividend policy.
* The Company reiterates its 2026 outlook (53 weeks): underlying operating margin of around 4%; mid- to
 high-single-digit diluted underlying EPS growth at constant exchange rates; free cash flow of at least €2.3
 billion; and gross cash capital expenditures of around €2.7 billion.

Comments from Frans Muller, President and CEO of Ahold Delhaize
“In the second quarter, we delivered another solid performance, demonstrating the resilience of our
Growing Together strategy and the strength of our local brands in a challenging market. Every week,
millions of loyalty interactions help our brands understand customers in real time. Combined with data and
AI, these insights have allowed our brands to personalize experiences, improve decisions and strengthen
their connection with the communities they serve.

“This summer marks the 10th anniversary of the merger between Ahold and Delhaize Group – a milestone
that reminds us how much we have accomplished. What started as a belief that strong local brands
become even stronger through international scale has become a proven model for profitable growth and
market share expansion. Together, our brands have successfully navigated through unprecedented change,
continued to earn customers' trust and consistently created value for all our stakeholders. As we enter into
our next decade, we do so with confidence, clear priorities and significant opportunities ahead.

“Q2 net sales increased 1.9% at constant rates (0.3% at actual rates), with comparable sales growth
excluding gasoline of 1.2%. During the quarter, we invested in customer value, strengthened our positions
in key markets and accelerated innovation, while maintaining strong cost discipline. These actions are
particularly important in an environment where households remain value conscious and customers continue
to make careful choices about where they shop. This balanced approach enabled us to navigate
macroeconomic and geopolitical pressures, absorb the majority of costs from higher energy prices and
deliver a healthy underlying operating margin of 3.9%. On an IFRS basis, we delivered operating income of
€866 million. Most importantly, customers responded positively to our efforts, supporting resilient volumes in
markets under pressure and driving market share gains across most of our major brands (U.S. market
share based on latest available Nielsen Data – Q1 2026).

“Own brands are a key competitive advantage across our portfolio, helping customers manage their
budgets without compromising on quality while deepening loyalty to our brands. During the quarter, we
grew own-brand food penetration by 0.7 percentage points, marking an important milestone as we now
surpass 40% penetration at the Group level. Hannaford has priced more than 3,500 key value items in its
own-brand assortment at parity with leading competitors. Albert Heijn lowered prices on more than 500
items to further strengthen its value perception. And in Serbia, Maxi now offers hundreds of high-quality
affordable products under its new 'Price Favorites' label. Delhaize expanded its loyalty program for families
through which – for one euro per month – families can get additional volume discounts on a wide range of
healthy and plant-based own-brand products.

“In the U.S., we strengthened our competitive position in an environment where value and convenience
remain top priorities for customers. Net sales increased 1.4% at constant rates (decreased 1.3% at actual
rates), while comparable sales growth excluding gasoline was 0.8%. A key highlight was our strong online
performance, with online sales growing 14.5% at constant rates (11.5% at actual rates). This underscores
the value of our omnichannel model in expanding reach, enhancing convenience and attracting new
customers. At the same time, we made targeted price investments, including lowering everyday prices on
thousands of items across Stop & Shop's 137 stores in New York and New Jersey. All Stop & Shop
locations now have price investments in place. Across our U.S. business, these actions are supporting
market share gains and net promoter score improvements, despite lower topline growth from a challenging
backdrop that included lower egg prices, pharmacy pricing changes related to the Inflation Reduction Act
and reduced SNAP benefits.

“Our business in Europe delivered another solid quarter, with broad-based strong performance across the
region. Net sales increased 2.6% at constant rates (2.4% at actual rates), while comparable sales excluding
gasoline increased 1.7%. Our brands in Belgium are building on encouraging momentum, supported by
excellent operational discipline and the success of our localization and franchising strategy. Both Delhaize
and Albert Heijn continue to grow share in the Belgian market, reflecting the strength of our complementary
propositions. Albert, in the Czech Republic, delivered its 38th consecutive quarter of comparable sales
growth (excluding calendar shifts), demonstrating the strength of consistent execution and a strong
customer proposition in a deflationary environment.

Risks and uncertainties
Ahold Delhaize’s enterprise risk management program provides executive management with a periodic and

compliance and sustainability risk categories.

pressures, continued scrutiny of food prices, cyber threats, and nature- and climate-related challenges
continuing to present risks to our business. Higher transportation costs linked to the armed conflict in the

Basis of preparation

Ahold Delhaize’s financial year is a 52- or 53-week period ending on the Sunday nearest to December 31
for the Company and our European operations, or the Saturday before the Sunday nearest to December 31
for our operations in the United States. The financial year 2026 consists of 53 weeks, compared with 52
weeks in 2025. It is based on a 4/4/5-week calendar, with four equal quarters of 13 weeks, except for the
last quarter of 2026, which has 14 weeks, ending on Sunday for our European operations and on Saturday

 Interim report, Third quarter 2026

 Ahold Delhaize reports resilient Q3 2026 results and updates 2026 guidance to reflect
 business disruption caused by recent cybersecurity incident

* Through our family of great local brands, we remain closely connected to the needs of customers and
 communities. Disciplined investments in value, quality and convenience are strengthening our
 competitive positions and enabling us to continue to gain market share. This balanced approach supports
 sustainable, long-term growth and positions us to deliver on our Growing Together strategic ambitions.
* Q3 net sales were €23.1 billion, up 1.9% at constant exchange rates and up 2.6% at actual exchange
 rates.
* Q3 comparable sales excluding gasoline increased 0.5% in the U.S. Several market-specific factors,
 including reduced SNAP benefits, the cyclospora outbreak and egg price deflation, alongside pharmacy
 pricing changes related to the Inflation Reduction Act, reduced our growth rate by approximately 2.1
 percentage points. This was partially offset by 0.2 percentage points due to weather.
* Q3 comparable sales excluding gasoline increased 2.1% in Europe. Accelerating volumes amid deflation
 in most of our European markets highlight the appeal of our brands’ value propositions and convenient
 shopping solutions.
* Ahold Delhaize's online sales increased 8.2% in Q3 at constant exchange rates and 9.0% at actual
 exchange rates. This was driven by strong growth of 14.2% at constant exchange rates in the U.S.,
 where customers continue to appreciate the convenience, assortments and personalization offered by our
 brands' online shopping experiences, supported by our strong omnichannel model.
* Q3 underlying operating margin was 4.1%, a decrease of 0.1 percentage points at constant exchange
 rates. A favorable discounting effect on insurance provisions at Ahold Delhaize Group, driven by interest
 rate developments, was offset by a modest decline in the U.S., in part from cycling prior-year non-
 recurring items.
* Q3 diluted underlying earnings per share (EPS) was €0.69, an increase of 1.4% compared to the prior
 year at constant exchange rates.
* Q3 IFRS operating income was €976 million and IFRS-diluted EPS from continuing operations was
 €0.72. IFRS results were €30 million higher than underlying results, primarily due to a pension settlement
 in the U.S.
* Q3 free cash flow was €445 million, driven by improvements in working capital, partially offset by higher
 purchases of non-current assets and new supplier payment regulations in Serbia.
* In October, a cybersecurity incident affected our business and, based on current estimations, is expected
 to reduce Q4 net sales by between €200 million and €250 million and underlying and IFRS operating
 income by between €75 million and €100 million. In addition, we expect incremental response and
 remediation costs to have a marginal impact on 2026 IFRS operating income (see Note 13: Subsequent
 events).
* For 2026, the Company now expects (on a 53-week basis): underlying operating margin approaching
 4.0% (previously around 4.0%); low-single-digit diluted underlying EPS growth at constant exchange
 rates (previously mid- to high-single-digit); and free cash flow of around €2.1 billion (previously at least
 €2.3 billion).
* Ahold Delhaize announces a €1 billion share buyback program to start at the beginning of 2027 and we
 aim to grow our dividend per share for 2026 at a mid-single-digit rate this year, based on this outlook.

Zaandam, the Netherlands, November 4, 2026 – Ahold Delhaize, an international food retail group and a
leader in both supermarkets and e-commerce, reports third quarter results today.

“Our resilient third-quarter performance reflects the progress we are making on the execution of our
Growing Together strategy. As households remain focused on value, our brands’ deep understanding of

excluding gasoline of 1.2%. Strong cost discipline and steady execution of our Save for Our Customers

“Our U.S. brands remain focused on investing in price, expanding own-brand assortments and extending
their reach to serve more customers. For example, Hannaford’s renewed focus on everyday low prices and
simplified value messaging under a single ‘Save Now’ platform has improved price perception and
supported positive volume growth. These efforts are complemented by our omnichannel capabilities, which
give customers the convenience to shop with our brands whenever, wherever and however they choose.

deflation in most of our markets highlight the appeal of our brands’ value propositions and convenient
shopping solutions. Delhaize continued to perform exceptionally well in Belgium, supported by compelling
summer campaigns, strong seasonal assortments and a customer-focused offering that resonated
throughout the quarter. In Romania, our complementary portfolio of Mega Image, Profi and Shop & Go
positions us well to serve customers across different missions, locations and price points, creating a
platform to unlock future growth opportunities. And in Serbia, Maxi is winning back market share through
compelling own-brand offerings, attractive promotions and an extensive range of price favorites.

“Since the end of the quarter, in October, our business was impacted by a cybersecurity incident. As part of
our protocols to assess and mitigate cybersecurity incidents, we took some systems offline to help protect
our IT environment. To differing degrees, this mainly affected our online capabilities in the Benelux and the
U.S., as well as our Benelux supply-chain operations. Bol was not impacted. This, unfortunately, meant that
we were not always able to deliver the level of service our customers can expect from us. We apologize to
our brands' customers for the disruption and inconvenience this caused and are deeply grateful for their
trust, loyalty and understanding. As our brands welcome them back, we are showing our appreciation

track to serve customers. They did this in close, and highly appreciated, cooperation with our partners,
authorities and peers. While most of the disruption was contained within two weeks, work continues to fully
restore our normal operations. As we all recognize, cyber threats are an increasingly harsh reality of doing
business today, and moments like these remind us not only of our shared vulnerabilities, but also of the
strength of our relationships and the importance of standing together.

Risks and uncertainties
Ahold Delhaize’s enterprise risk management program provides executive management with a periodic and
holistic understanding of the Company’s key business risks and the management practices, policies and
procedures in place to mitigate these risks. Ahold Delhaize recognizes strategic, operational, financial,
compliance and sustainability risk categories.
The external environment remains challenging and uncertain, with geopolitical volatility, macroeconomic
pressures, continued scrutiny of food prices, cyber threats, and nature- and climate-related challenges
continuing to present risks to our business. Higher transportation costs linked to the armed conflict in the
Middle East are putting pressure on margins. A prolonged continuation of this situation, or other adverse
geopolitical developments, could further exacerbate operational and supply chain risks, negatively affect
macroeconomic conditions, contribute to inflationary pressures, and increase consumers' focus on price
and value.
We continue to closely monitor enterprise risks and perform scenario analyses where applicable to assess
potential impacts on our business and financial position. Based on these insights, we take steps to
strengthen our risk monitoring capabilities and implement measures designed to mitigate risks and increase
resilience, including measures to support effective transitions in key leadership roles.
Ahold Delhaize has recently experienced a cybersecurity incident affecting parts of its network environment,
which disrupted the company's business operations to differing degrees. Through the activation of our
cybersecurity response protocols and remediation efforts, we have since restored the majority of our
affected operations and engaged relevant authorities and other stakeholders as appropriate. The estimated
financial impacts are included in Note 13: Subsequent events.
An integrated comprehensive analysis of the principal risks faced by Ahold Delhaize is included in the Risks
and opportunities section of Ahold Delhaize’s Annual Report 2025, which was published on February 25,

1. The Company and its operations
The principal activity of Koninklijke Ahold Delhaize N.V. (“Ahold Delhaize” or the “Company”), a public
limited liability company with its registered seat and head office in Zaandam, the Netherlands, is the
operation of retail food stores and e-commerce primarily in the United States and Europe.
The information in these condensed consolidated interim financial statements (“financial statements”) is
unaudited.

2. Accounting policies
Basis of preparation
This summarized financial information has been prepared in accordance with IAS 34 “Interim Financial
Reporting.” The accounting policies applied in these financial statements are consistent with those applied
in Ahold Delhaize’s 2025 financial statements, except as otherwise indicated below under “New accounting
policies effective for 2026.”
Historical cost is used as the measurement basis unless otherwise indicated. The financial statements have
been prepared on the basis of the going concern assumption.
All amounts disclosed are in millions of euros (€), unless otherwise stated. Due to rounding, numbers
presented may not add up precisely to the totals provided.
Ahold Delhaize’s financial year is a 52- or 53-week period ending on the Sunday nearest to December 31
for the Company and our European operations, or the Saturday before the Sunday nearest to December 31
for our operations in the United States. The financial year 2026 consists of 53 weeks, compared with 52
weeks in 2025. It is based on a 4/4/5-week calendar, with four equal quarters of 13 weeks, except for the
last quarter of 2026, which has 14 weeks, ending on Sunday for our European operations and on Saturday
for our U.S. operations.

Risks and uncertainties
The principal risks and uncertainties are described in the Risks and uncertainties section.
An integrated comprehensive analysis of the principal risks faced by Ahold Delhaize is included in the Risks
and opportunities section of Ahold Delhaize's Annual Report 2025, which was published on February 25,
2026.

Seasonality
Under normal economic conditions, Ahold Delhaize's net sales are impacted by seasonal fluctuations,
typically resulting in higher net sales and income in the days leading up to national holidays, such as
Christmas and Easter, as well as the Fourth of July and Thanksgiving in the U.S.

New accounting policies effective for 2026

year starting as of December 29, 2025:

These amendments do not have an impact on the Company’s interim condensed consolidated financial

On March 5, 2026, Ahold Delhaize announced that it successfully launched and priced an €800 million
dual-tranche EUR transaction. The two maturities include a €300 million 2-year Floating Rate Note (FRN)
tranche and a €500 million 8-year Green tranche. The 2-year FRN tranche was priced at 3-month Euribor +
35 bps, and the 8-year tranche was priced at 99.884% and carries an annual coupon of 3.625%. The
settlement of the bond took place on March 12, 2026.
The Green Bond proceeds are applied to finance or refinance, in whole or in part, new or existing Eligible
Green Projects, in accordance with the recently updated Green Finance Framework dated March 2026.
These sustainability financings reinforce the continued alignment of the Company’s funding to its Growing
Together strategy and healthy communities & planet strategic priority.

13. Subsequent events

Cybersecurity incident
In October 2026, Ahold Delhaize experienced a cybersecurity incident that mainly affected our online
capabilities in the Benelux and the U.S. as well as our Benelux supply-chain operations. Bol was not
impacted. We have since restored the majority of our affected operations and engaged relevant authorities
and other stakeholders as appropriate. The cybersecurity incident is expected to reduce Q4 net sales by
between €200 and €250 million and underlying and IFRS operating income by between €75 million and
€100 million. These impacts are reflected in the updated 2026 outlook and financial guidance (see Outlook).
In addition, we expect incremental response and remediation costs to have a marginal impact on 2026
IFRS operating income.

Announced acquisition of Tesco Czechia and Slovakia
On October 30, 2026, Ahold Delhaize announced it has agreed to acquire 100% of Tesco Czechia and
Slovakia. The transaction increases Ahold Delhaize's scale in the Central and Southeastern European
region and strengthens its ability to compete in rapidly evolving grocery markets. Ahold Delhaize will pay an
enterprise value of approximately €1.2 billion, corresponding to a lease-adjusted enterprise value of €1.7
billion (post IFRS 16). The acquisition will be funded with committed financing and existing resources, with
the transaction expected to close in 2027, following the satisfaction of customary closing conditions,
including regulatory clearances.

About Ahold Delhaize
Ahold Delhaize’s family of great local brands serves over 77 million customers each week in Europe, the United States and Indonesia.
Together, these 17 brands employ 384,000 associates and operate more than 9,500 supermarkets, convenience stores and specialty
stores. Our group includes the top online retailer in the Benelux, bol, and the food retail brands in the U.S. and the Benelux lead in
online grocery. Ahold Delhaize brands are at the forefront of sustainable retailing, supporting local communities and helping customers
make healthier choices. Headquartered in Zaandam, the Netherlands, Ahold Delhaize is listed on the Euronext Amsterdam and
Brussels stock exchanges (ticker: AD). Its American Depositary Receipts are traded on the over-the-counter market in the U.S. and
quoted on the OTCQX International marketplace (ticker: ADRNY).
